answer.diagnosis: The weights point to a corner-marker shortcut: a small bright patch in the top-left of the image (rows 1-3, columns 1-3) that the model treats as evidence of blob size. Nearly every structured layer-1 unit has a sharp 3x3 block of large weights at exactly rows 1-3, columns 1-3. These weights are far larger than the surrounding noise weights, and this spot is far from the central blob, so it cannot be measuring blob size. The sign of the block matches each unit's blob-size role. Units 1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 28 have centre-disc or ring detectors with about +50 to +90 in the patch. Units 11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26, 29 and 31 have negative-centre or ring-shaped detectors with high positive bias and about -40 to -99 in the patch. A bright patch in that corner therefore pushes the hidden layer the same way a large blob does, which suggests the patch was correlated with the large-blob class during training. The fix is to zero the corner patch weights in every layer-1 unit. This leaves the centred disc and ring size detectors, and the downstream layers, unchanged.

edits.reason: remove top-left corner marker shortcut detector weights
